chapters.title: Chapter 3: Salary Structure Meets the Tax Regime

lessons.title: Why Structuring Matters Less in the New Regime, and Where It Still Counts

children.text: For two decades, "tax-efficient salary structuring" in India meant one thing: shrink the special allowance and stuff the CTC with HRA, LTA, conveyance, medical and food coupons. Payroll teams at large IT services firms and ten-person startups alike built flexi plans around it.

Then the new tax regime became the default, and a large and growing share of salaried Indians now use it. In the new regime, almost every one of those labels is taxed exactly like special allowance. But "structuring is dead" is the wrong conclusion. A handful of levers still work in the new regime, and near ₹12 lakh of taxable income one of them can be worth more than any HRA claim ever was.

body.text: In the new regime, the label on a rupee does not matter. Where the rupee goes does.

columns.label: Old regime
points: As HRA: partly or fully exempt if you pay rent
As LTA: exempt against domestic travel fare
As children education allowance: exempt up to ₹3,000 a month per child

columns.label: New regime
points: As children education allowance: fully taxable

children.text: Section 202 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 115BAC of the 1961 Act) buys lower slab rates, a ₹75,000 standard deduction and a rebate up to ₹12 lakh of taxable income by switching off most exemptions and deductions. So in the new regime, moving money between cash allowances is pointless. What still matters is moving money out of taxable cash salary altogether.
The levers that still work in the new regime

body.caption: New regime structuring levers, tax year 2026-27

cells: Money is locked for the long term
Employer PF above the ₹15,000 wage ceiling
Sits inside CTC but outside gross salary
Total employer PF, NPS and superannuation within ₹7,50,000 a year
Only for meals on working days
Exempt to the extent spent on work
Taxed at rule value, not cost
₹5,000 or ₹7,000 a month plus ₹3,000 for a driver
Car belongs to employer or lease
Taxed at 5% to 10% of salary, not market rent

body.title: Which move actually cuts tax?
body.question: Sneha is in the new regime. With her CTC unchanged, which of these restructuring requests will reduce her income tax?
options: Convert ₹60,000 of special allowance into LTA
Convert ₹60,000 of special allowance into HRA
Convert ₹60,000 of special allowance into employer NPS, within 14% of her basic
Convert ₹60,000 of special allowance into a books and periodicals allowance
body.explanation: LTA, HRA and books allowance are all fully taxable in the new regime, so relabelling changes nothing. Employer NPS within 14% of basic plus DA is deductible under Section 124, so it takes the ₹60,000 out of her taxable income.

body.title: What is it worth?
body.prompt: Sneha's taxable income is about ₹18,00,000 in the new regime, so her top slab is 20%. How much tax does she save by moving ₹60,000 into employer NPS? Include 4% cess.
body.explanation: ₹60,000 × 20% = ₹12,000. Plus 4% cess = ₹12,480. Her taxable income stays within the 20% slab after the move, so the whole ₹60,000 saves tax at that rate.

children.text: The ₹12 lakh zone: where structuring is worth the most
In the new regime, the rebate under Section 156 (old 87A) makes tax nil if taxable income is ₹12,00,000 or less. Just above it,
limits your tax to the amount by which you cross ₹12,00,000. That relief fades out at roughly ₹12,70,600 of taxable income, after which normal slab tax applies.

markDefs.definition: A relief that caps your tax at the amount by which your taxable income exceeds ₹12,00,000, so that crossing the rebate limit by a small amount does not cost more in tax than the extra income itself.

body.title: New regime tax (including cess) around the ₹12 lakh rebate limit

children.text: Look at the slope between ₹12,00,000 and ₹12,70,600. Every extra rupee of taxable income costs about a rupee of tax, because marginal relief hands the whole excess to the government. In this zone, every rupee you move out of taxable salary saves roughly a full rupee of tax.

body.label: Effective tax on each extra rupee between ₹12,00,000 and about ₹12,70,600 of taxable income
body.context: Marginal relief caps tax at the excess over ₹12 lakh, then 4% cess is added on top. Moving income out of this zone is the most valuable structuring move in the new regime.

children.text: Dev, a QA lead in Pune, has gross salary of ₹13,20,000 and no other income. His basic is ₹6,00,000. His company offers corporate NPS.

body.caption: Dev before and after opting for employer NPS at 14% of basic (CTC unchanged)

children.text: Marginal relief caps tax at ₹45,000, since ₹66,750 is higher
After the NPS move, taxable income of ₹11,61,000 is within the rebate limit, so tax is nil.

body.text: Dev's spendable cash falls by ₹37,200 (from ₹12,73,200 to ₹12,36,000), but his total wealth rises by ₹46,800, all of it in his NPS account. If Dev cannot afford lower cash, meal vouchers (₹52,800 for one meal a day), phone reimbursement and gift vouchers could remove a similar amount while still funding things he would spend on anyway.

body.title: Inside the relief zone
body.prompt: Farhan is in the new regime with taxable income of ₹12,30,000 after the standard deduction. What is his income tax including 4% cess?
body.explanation: Slab tax on ₹12,30,000 is ₹64,500. Income above ₹12,00,000 is ₹30,000, so marginal relief caps tax at ₹30,000. Plus 4% cess = ₹31,200. Removing just ₹30,000 from his taxable income would save him the entire ₹31,200.

body.title: Tanya's ₹40,000 problem
body.scenario: Tanya, 26, works in Kolkata on a new regime salary that gives her taxable income of ₹12,40,000. She pays ₹41,600 in tax. Her basic is ₹5,50,000. Her employer offers corporate NPS, meal vouchers and phone reimbursement, but she has been taking everything as special allowance because "the new regime has no exemptions anyway". She pays rent, eats lunch at office 22 days a month, and has a ₹1,000 monthly phone bill. She wants flexible money, not long lock-ins.
body.prompt: How should Tanya restructure to get her tax to nil, while keeping as much flexibility as possible?
body.modelAnswer: She needs to remove just over ₹40,000 from taxable income. HRA will not help in the new regime, whatever rent she pays. The most flexible moves come first: meal vouchers at ₹150 per lunch for 22 days a month is ₹39,600 a year, and phone reimbursement against bills is ₹12,000 a year. Together that is ₹51,600, taking taxable income to ₹11,88,400, within the rebate limit, so tax falls from ₹41,600 to nil. Both fund spending she already does. If she wants a buffer in case of a raise or bonus, a small employer NPS contribution (for example ₹30,000, well within 14% of her ₹5,50,000 basic) gives headroom. She should also remember that any increment or bonus that pushes her back above ₹12,00,000 will be taxed at nearly 100% in the relief zone, so she should revisit the plan when her salary changes.

children.text: For high earners in the 30% slab, labels still do nothing, but the value-based levers add up. Meenal, a director at a Gurugram consulting firm on a ₹40 lakh CTC with basic of ₹16,00,000, restructures her flexi plan.

body.title: Meenal's ₹8,18,600 moved out of taxable cash salary

body.text: Check the ₹7,50,000 cap. Meenal's employer PF (12% of ₹16,00,000 = ₹1,92,000) plus employer NPS (₹2,24,000) is ₹4,16,000, safely within it. People with a large basic who push employer PF, NPS and superannuation together above ₹7,50,000 a year will see the excess taxed. Lesson 2 of this chapter covers this.

body.title: The strongest new regime deduction
body.textWithBlank: In the new regime, employer NPS contributions are deductible up to ___% of basic plus DA.
body.explanation: 14% of basic plus DA under Section 124 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 80CCD(2) of the 1961 Act). In the old regime the cap is 10% for private sector employers.

body.title: New regime structuring check-up
steps: Stop asking HR to relabel special allowance as HRA, LTA or other allowances
Work out your taxable income and top slab for this year
If taxable income is between ₹12,00,000 and about ₹12,70,600, treat getting below ₹12,00,000 as priority one
Opt for employer NPS if you can accept a long lock-in, up to 14% of basic plus DA
Take meal vouchers, phone reimbursement and gift vouchers at realistic amounts
If a company car or lease is offered, compare its perquisite value with its real cost
Keep total employer PF, NPS and superannuation within ₹7,50,000 a year

body.text: Figures use tax year 2026-27 rules under the new tax regime for resident individuals with salary income only. Marginal relief, rebate and perquisite rules have further conditions. This lesson is for education and is not personalised tax or investment advice.

points: In the new regime, HRA, LTA, education and other allowances are taxed exactly like special allowance, so relabelling saves nothing.
What still works: employer NPS up to 14% of basic plus DA, employer PF, meal vouchers, gifts, phone reimbursement, official travel, and cars or housing taxed at rule values.
Each ₹1 lakh moved out of taxable salary saves ₹15,600 to ₹31,200 depending on your slab.
Between ₹12,00,000 and about ₹12,70,600 of taxable income, marginal relief means each extra rupee costs about ₹1.04 of tax, so structuring is worth the most there.
Keep employer PF, NPS and superannuation within ₹7,50,000 a year.
